skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python 3.10 code through the inference.sh sandbox with common data, web, media, document, and automation libraries preinstalled.
skill.summary: Execute Python scripts through inference.sh with common analysis, scraping, and media libraries.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Most external command detections are false positives from Markdown code fences and inline package names. The audit confirms a critical pipe-to-shell installer command, intentional outbound network examples, and a high-risk remote arbitrary Python execution capability. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Pipe-to-shell installer in the Quick Start
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl pipe sh with package-manager installation steps, a checksum-pinned download, or a manual review step before execution.
Document that code, inputs, and outputs are sent to inference.sh, and warn users not to include secrets or private datasets.
Add guidance to limit scraping and API calls to approved targets, and avoid transmitting credentials or personal data.
Narrow the run any Python script language to approved, non-sensitive workloads and link to sandbox controls.

semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to submit arbitrary Python code to infsh/python-executor and advertises automation for any Python script. This can expose code, input data, and outputs to a third-party execution service.

content.user_title: Run Python Code in a Remote Sandbox
content.value_statement: Teams need quick Python execution without preparing local environments. This skill runs code through inference.sh with libraries for analysis, scraping, media, and automation.
actual_capabilities: Uses libraries such as pandas, matplotlib, Pillow, requests, Selenium, and Playwright.
Returns files saved under outputs, including charts, CSVs, PDFs, videos, and 3D models.
Supports timeout control from 1 to 300 seconds.
Offers default 8GB RAM and high-memory 16GB RAM variants.
Handles data analysis, scraping, media processing, PDF generation, and API calls.
limitations: Runs CPU-only and does not provide GPU or dedicated ML runtimes.
Requires inference.sh CLI access and an authenticated account.
Sends code and inputs to an external execution service.
Non-interactive tasks should save files instead of opening UI windows.

use_cases.title: Analyze Operational Data
use_cases.description: Clean a dataset, compute summaries, and return charts or CSV outputs from a managed Python environment.

use_cases.title: Automate Public API Workflows
use_cases.description: Call approved APIs, transform responses, and generate files without configuring a local Python runtime.

use_cases.title: Create Media And Documents
use_cases.description: Generate images, simple videos, PDFs, and 3D files using preinstalled Python libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Small Python Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python task, explain the result, and return any saved output files.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor with pandas to clean the attached sales data, summarize trends, and save a chart under outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Process Media Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to resize these images, build a contact sheet, and return the saved image files.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a Report Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch approved public API data, transform it, create a PDF report, and return generated files. Do not include secrets.

output_examples.input: Analyze a sales spreadsheet and create a bar chart.
output_examples.output: A concise trend summary plus a saved chart file that compares sales by person or period.

output_examples.input: Collect titles from an approved public web page.
output_examples.output: A short table of extracted page information with notes about any missing or malformed fields.

output_examples.input: Create a PDF report from processed data.
output_examples.output: A downloadable report with summary sections, charts, and source notes.

best_practices: Review code before execution and remove secrets, tokens, and private datasets.
Set explicit timeouts and save generated files under outputs.
Limit network calls to approved public URLs and follow site policies.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installers directly into a shell in automated workflows.
Running untrusted or private code without review.
Using scraping examples against sites without permission.

faq.question: What does this skill execute?
faq.answer: It executes Python 3.10 code through the inference.sh python-executor app.

faq.question: Does it run code locally?
faq.answer: No. The examples use the inference.sh CLI to run code in a remote execution environment.

faq.question: Which libraries are available?
faq.answer: The skill lists NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, requests, BeautifulSoup, Selenium, Playwright, Pillow, OpenCV, MoviePy, and more.

faq.question: Can it return generated files?
faq.answer: Yes. Files saved under outputs are returned, including charts, CSVs, PDFs, videos, and 3D models.

faq.question: What should users avoid sending?
faq.answer: Users should avoid secrets, credentials, private datasets, and proprietary code unless their organization approves the service.

faq.question: Why is installation a security concern?
faq.answer: The Quick Start pipes a remote installer into a shell, which can execute unexpected code if the installer source is compromised.
